To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the consistent anisotrpic Wiener filtering (CAWF) algorithm is an efficient method for audio source separation, (2) the CAWF algorithm outperforms the state of the art for audio source separation in terms of both quality and speed.

(1) we propose to improve the Wiener filtering technique used for audio source separation by accounting for the phase consistency in the STFT and by modeling the source phase with an anisotropic Gaussian distribution, (2) the proposed technique leads to results similar to or slightly better than the state of the art, and (3) the proposed technique is much faster than the state of art, and is thus well suited for real-time applications.

(1) we propose to use the STFT consistency to improve the separation of sources that overlap in the time-frequency domain; (2) this consistency is exploited in an algorithm that is based on an anisotropic Gaussian model of the sources; (3) this approach is shown to be effective in the case of musical mixtures.
